---
# TEMPLATE: book, course, training resource or community
# Copy this whole folder into books_training/, rename the folder, and fill in the fields below.
# See templates/README.md for step-by-step instructions and examples.
# For a collection of YouTube recordings, use templates/recordings_collection/ instead.
# Lines starting with # are comments - you can leave them in or delete them.

title: "Replace this with the name of the book, course, resource or community"

categories:
  # 1. Always keep this one:
  - Courses and Training or Reference Materials
  # 2. Keep EXACTLY ONE of these - it decides which section of the Books, Training & Communities page the entry appears in:
  - Books                       # Books section (listed as healthcare-specific unless you add General Open Analytics)
  - Courses                     # Training > Courses - also needs Synchronous and/or Asynchronous (see 3.)
  - Interactive Learning Tools  # Training > Interactive learning tools
  - Reference Sites             # Training > Reference sites
  - Recorded Talks              # Training > Recorded webinars and conference talks
  - Communities                 # Communities section
  # 3. Only for Courses - keep one or both:
  - Synchronous                 # taught live at set times
  - Asynchronous                # self-paced materials
  # 4. Only for Books - keep if they apply:
  - General Open Analytics      # the book isn't specific to healthcare
  - Paid Resources              # the book has to be bought or needs a subscription (also add the paid icon to project-type below)
  # 5. Optionally, add topic tags from templates/packages_projects_tools_permitted_categories.csv, e.g.:
  # - Service Planning

tool-language: # The language(s) the resource teaches or uses, from templates/packages_projects_tools_permitted_languages.csv.
               # Use N/A if it isn't about a particular language (e.g. most communities).
  - N/A
  # - Python
  # - R

# Rating of the resource's quality and how well it's maintained - see "Choosing a rating" in templates/README.md.
# Remove the # from the start of ONE of these lines. Keep the quote marks exactly as they are.
# Use N/A for things a rating doesn't suit, such as communities or collections from many different people.
# status: '<span style="color: #D18B12FF">Gold</span>'
# status: '<span style="color: #888888FF">Silver</span>'
# status: '<span style="color: #893400FF">Bronze</span>'
# status: 'N/A'

image: my_image.png # Image for the listing card and the top of the entry, e.g. a book cover or a screenshot of the course homepage.
                    # Put it in this folder and give just its filename. If you don't have one, delete this line.

author: # Who wrote or runs the resource. Add a "- name:" block for each author or organisation.
        # affiliation, orcid and url are optional - delete any you don't need.
  - name: Author or Organisation Name
    affiliation: Their organisation or institution
    orcid: 0000-0000-0000-0000
    url: https://link-to-their-profile-or-website

date: "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+00:00" # REQUIRED: when the entry was added or last updated, e.g. "2026-01-31T10:00:00+00:00".
                                  # Used to order the homepage's "Most recently added or updated" list. Don't use `today` or `last-modified`.

pub-info:
  # Icons shown after the title:
  #   - fa-hospital: made by people in the NHS, public health or other healthcare/government organisations
  #   - fa-user-graduate: made by people in academia
  #   - fa-sterling-sign: REQUIRED for Paid Resources, alongside any other icons
  # Remove the # from the start of the line that applies. If none apply, leave them all commented out.
  # project-type: <i class="fa-solid fa-user-graduate"></i>
  # project-type: <i class="fa-solid fa-hospital"></i>
  # project-type: <i class="fa-solid fa-user-graduate"></i> <i class="fa-solid fa-sterling-sign" title="Paid resource"></i>

  rationale-for-status: | # Why you gave this rating. For N/A, briefly say why it isn't rated.
    Replace this with the reasoning for the rating.

  entry-author: # Optional: you, the person writing this Atlas entry. Delete this block if you'd rather not be named.
    - name: Your Name
      url: https://github.com/your-username # Optional: GitHub profile, website, ORCID or similar

  abstract: | # Summary shown on the listing card and at the top of the entry. Aim for 50-200 words.
    Replace this with a short description of the resource: what it covers, who it's for, and how it's delivered.

  # Buttons shown on the listing card and the entry. Fill in the urls that apply.
  # Any link left with an empty url is hidden, so you can leave unused ones or delete them.
  # To add another, copy a block and change the name, url and icon (see templates/README.md for icons).
  links:
  - name: Website
    url:
    icon: fa-solid fa-globe
  - name: eBook
    url:
    icon: fa-solid fa-book
  - name: Module
    url:
    icon: fa-solid fa-book
  - name: Code
    url:
    icon: fa-brands fa-github
  - name: YouTube
    url:
    icon: fa-brands fa-youtube
  - name: LinkedIn
    url:
    icon: fa-brands fa-linkedin
---
